symptom: Two modules declare the same artifact at different versions (ExcelImporter commons-lang3 3.18.0, CommunityCommons 3.20.0): `sync-java-deps --check` fails with `missing  org.apache.commons:commons-lang3:3.18.0`, the sync deletes that jar and errors `sync finished but 1 dependency/dependencies are still missing from vendorlib/`, and `run --local` stops at `Resolving 1 managed Java dependency` on every start (#1450)
cause: `UnvendoredJarDependencies` checked every declaration for `<artifact>-<version>.jar`, but `mx sync-java-dependencies` runs Gradle over all modules at once and its conflict resolution vendors only the newest version per group:artifact — the older coordinate can never appear, so the postcondition was unsatisfiable
insight: A gate that checks the sync's postcondition must check what the sync PRODUCES, not what the model declares — and the two differ exactly where Gradle resolves a conflict. The tell in the report was a sync that 'succeeded' and deleted the jar it then called missing: an unsatisfiable postcondition, not a failed download. Measured on 11.12.1 with `mxcli new` + two modules: vendorlib/ gets commons-lang3-3.20.0.jar only; pre-fix binary prints the reported error verbatim, fixed one passes. Versions must compare Gradle's way (numeric parts numerically, 1.0-beta < 1.0): a string compare picks 3.9.0 over 3.20.0. To run mx sync here, Gradle needs the proxy as JVM props (JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS -Dhttps.proxyHost/Port) — otherwise mx says 'Failed to find some hosts', which is not a Maven outage. The per-module Note in `alter module … add jar dependency` (executor `warnUnvendoredJarDependencies`) still checks one module's declarations and can name a superseded coordinate
